records.definition: ADU type describes whether the unit is detached, attached to the home, or a Junior ADU within the home.
records.whyAsked: The type can affect which address, meter, permitting, and service questions need confirmation.
records.findIt: Review the permit description or ask the city or county planning department or the project contractor.

records.definition: Electric service is the connection that delivers electricity from PG&E equipment to the property.
records.whyAsked: The service arrangement can affect which project questions, photos, and documents may be relevant.
records.findIt: Look at whether visible wires reach the property from a pole or whether the route is below ground.

records.definition: The electrical panel, or breaker box, distributes electricity to circuits in the home and contains the circuit breakers.
records.whyAsked: The planned work may affect the existing panel, but a load calculation and field review are needed before deciding what changes apply.
records.findIt: The panel is commonly located on an exterior wall, in a garage, or in a utility area.
records.safetyNote: Do not remove the panel cover. Ask a licensed electrician for help identifying equipment.

records.definition: A load calculation is a licensed electrician's calculation of how much electrical power the property and planned equipment may need.
records.whyAsked: The calculation helps a licensed electrician evaluate whether planned equipment may fit the existing panel and service.
records.findIt: A licensed electrician usually prepares the calculation using the property's equipment and planned electrical loads.

records.definition: The main breaker is the large switch that controls electricity for the whole home.
records.whyAsked: The breaker rating can help a licensed electrician understand the home's existing capacity and whether more review may be useful.
records.findIt: The rating is often printed on the largest breaker.
records.safetyNote: Do not remove the panel cover. Ask a licensed electrician if the rating is unclear.

records.definition: Overhead service reaches the property through visible wires supported by poles.
records.whyAsked: An overhead route can call for different photos and site information than an underground route.
records.findIt: From a safe location, look for visible wires running from a utility pole toward the building.
records.safetyNote: Do not approach, touch, or work near electrical wires or utility equipment.

records.definition: A panel cut sheet is the manufacturer's specification sheet showing the panel's ratings and equipment details.
records.whyAsked: The document may help confirm equipment information for higher-amperage or multi-meter layouts.
records.findIt: Ask the equipment supplier or electrician for the manufacturer's specification sheet, or use a clear photo of an allowed rating label when applicable.

records.definition: The panel rating is the maximum electrical capacity shown on the panel's label.
records.whyAsked: The rating provides one input for comparing the existing equipment with the project being considered.
records.findIt: Look for a manufacturer label inside the panel door.
records.safetyNote: Do not remove covers to find the label. Ask a licensed electrician if the label is unclear.

records.definition: The permit authority is the city or county office responsible for permits and inspections for the project.
records.whyAsked: Local permits, address assignments, and inspection releases can affect which information needs confirmation and when work can proceed.
records.findIt: Check the project's permit documents or contact the city or county building or planning department.

records.definition: A single-line diagram is a simplified drawing showing how major electrical equipment connects.
records.whyAsked: The drawing may be requested for larger services or multi-meter layouts.
records.findIt: A licensed electrician or electrical designer usually prepares it; a hand-drawn version may be acceptable only when the applicable process allows it.

records.definition: Underground service reaches the property through electrical equipment and wiring below ground.
records.whyAsked: An underground route can call for different site questions than an overhead route.
records.findIt: If no service wires are visible overhead, the service may be underground, but the arrangement may still need confirmation.
records.safetyNote: Do not open utility equipment or dig to locate electrical facilities.
